objective: Test literature-backed realized-volatility model structure on a historical Nikkei 225 minute proxy before spending effort on formal OSE/JNU intraday validation.

evidence.paper: Asai & McAleer (2017) Forecasting the volatility of Nikkei 225 futures
evidence.implication: High-frequency information and asymmetry matter; direct long-memory models can be biased.

evidence.paper: Maki & Ota (2021) Impacts of asymmetry on forecasting realized volatility in Japanese stock markets
evidence.implication: Use 5-minute RV; compare HAR benchmark with leverage and realized-semivariance asymmetry. Do not prioritize asymmetric-jump extensions.

transformation.resample: 5-minute last price within AM and PM separately

method_proxy_pass: At least one asymmetric challenger beats HAR_RV on both full-OOS QLIKE and MSE
Improvement direction is not contradicted in the 2015-2018 subperiod
Block-bootstrap probability of positive loss improvement >= 0.95 for at least one primary metric
promotion_rule.formal_jnu_validation: Prohibited. Requires true OSE/JNU intraday data with rules frozen.

data_quality.rule: Fail/drop partial days before model fitting; threshold fixed before the first cloud run.
